# Implementation Plan: Multimodal Enterprise RAG UI

**Branch**: `002-multimodal-enterprise-rag` | **Date**: 2025-10-27 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/002-multimodal-enterprise-rag/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan was generated by the `/speckit.plan` command based on comprehensive technical research.

## Summary

The Multimodal Enterprise RAG UI is a modern web-based interface that provides users with a two-panel layout for document management and intelligent search. The system supports drag-and-drop file uploads for PDF, TXT, JPG, PNG, MP3, and MP4 files, processes them in real-time, and enables natural language querying with comprehensive answers, source citations, knowledge graph exploration, and performance evaluation metrics.

**Technical Approach**: Next.js 15 with App Router + TypeScript frontend consuming comprehensive FastAPI backend microservices with API-first design, WebSocket real-time updates, responsive design for desktop/tablet/mobile, server-side rendering, and comprehensive error handling.

**Backend Architecture**: Microservices-based architecture with 9 core services (API Gateway, Document Management, Search, Knowledge Graph, Evaluation, Processing Pipeline, Analytics, User Management, Real-time Communications) supporting multi-modal file processing, hybrid search, and RAG evaluation.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.3+ with Next.js 15 and React 18.2+
**Primary Dependencies**: Next.js 15, React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, react-dropzone, vis-network, framer-motion, Axios, @tanstack/react-query, Zustand
**Storage**: Comprehensive microservices backend with PostgreSQL (metadata & user data), Neo4j (knowledge graph), Qdrant (vector store), Redis (cache & message queues), and multi-modal file storage
**Testing**: Jest + React Testing Library + Cypress for E2E
**Target Platform**: Web application (desktop, tablet, mobile browsers)
**Project Type**: Full-stack web application with Next.js 15 App Router, SSR capabilities, and real-time features
**Performance Goals**: <2s query response time, <5min file processing, <1s graph rendering for 500 nodes
**Constraints**: 50MB file size limit, 5GB user storage quota, 99.5% uptime with 2-hour monthly maintenance windows
**Scale/Scope**: 500 concurrent users, 10+ file types, real-time processing with WebSocket updates

## Current Implementation Status

**✅ PRODUCTION READY** - The Next.js 15 frontend is fully implemented and deployed at `http://localhost:3000`

### Next.js 15 Implementation Features:
- **App Router**: Modern file-based routing with layouts and nested routes
- **Server-Side Rendering (SSR)**: Enhanced SEO and performance with server components
- **API Routes**: Built-in API endpoints for backend integration
- **Built-in Optimizations**: Automatic code splitting, image optimization, and caching
- **Advanced Configuration**: Custom webpack configuration for file handling, CORS headers, and security
- **Development Experience**: Fast refresh, TypeScript integration, and comprehensive tooling

### Implemented Components:
- **Complete UI**: All major components implemented with shadcn/ui design system

- **Search Interface**: Real-time search with filtering and results display
- **Knowledge Graph Visualization**: Interactive network graphs with vis-network
- **Authentication**: Login/register pages with JWT integration
- **Responsive Design**: Mobile-first approach with Tailwind CSS
- **State Management**: Zustand for global state, @tanstack/react-query for server state
- **Testing Infrastructure**: Jest, React Testing Library, and Playwright E2E tests

### Deployment Ready:
- **Build Configuration**: Optimized production builds with Next.js 15
- **Environment Variables**: Proper configuration management
- **API Integration**: Seamless backend communication with FastAPI services
- **Performance**: Optimized for production with caching and code splitting

**Rationale**: This structure maintains the existing comprehensive microservices backend while leveraging a production-ready Next.js 15 frontend. The Next.js 15 App Router provides modern file-based routing, server-side rendering, and built-in optimizations that enhance performance and SEO. The API-first design ensures clear separation of concerns: backend handles all business logic, data processing, and algorithms; Next.js frontend provides exceptional user experience with SSR, automatic code splitting, and optimized asset delivery. This architecture enables independent development, testing, and deployment while ensuring robust integration through well-defined OpenAPI specifications and real-time WebSocket communications.

## Complexity Tracking

*No constitutional violations - all requirements satisfied within standard web application complexity.*

| Aspect | Complexity Level | Justification |
|--------|------------------|---------------|
| Frontend Framework | LOW-MEDIUM | Next.js 15 with App Router reduces complexity through built-in routing, SSR, and optimizations |
| API Integration | LOW | All backend endpoints already implemented and documented with Next.js API rewrites |
| State Management | LOW-MEDIUM | Zustand + @tanstack/react-query provide efficient state management with less boilerplate |
| Real-time Features | LOW-MEDIUM | WebSocket integration simplified by Next.js architecture and built-in optimizations |
| File Upload | LOW-MEDIUM | Drag-and-drop with progress tracking, simplified by Next.js file handling configuration |
| Graph Visualization | HIGH | Interactive knowledge graph with filtering and layout algorithms (inherent complexity remains) |
| Responsive Design | LOW | Tailwind CSS with Next.js optimization simplifies responsive implementation |
| Testing | MEDIUM | Comprehensive testing with Jest, React Testing Library, and Playwright E2E |

**Overall Assessment**: **LOW-MEDIUM COMPLEXITY** - Next.js 15 significantly reduces frontend complexity through built-in optimizations, routing, and developer experience improvements. The framework handles many concerns automatically (code splitting, SSR, routing), allowing focus on business logic. All remaining complexity is justified by enterprise requirements and no simpler alternatives would meet the specification while maintaining production quality.
